what: segment.rs copy(): when a lane's open segment is full it makes the next one with cap = open.next_cap.max(self.first) and puts the copy at 0 without checking len <= cap, so any copy with cap < len <= max/4 trips debug_assert at segment.rs:367 (`at + bytes.len() <= segment.cap`) and in release writes past the segment. Seen from memo.rs:354 copy_value of a LoadFile (read_file) on a FRESH daemon building a crate that depends on object 0.39.1, and on every rebuild after an edit or a daemon restart. Fix: cap = open.next_cap.max(self.first).max(len.next_multiple_of(SEGMENT_ALIGN)) (and a unit test: an open lane segment, then a copy bigger than next_cap). Repro tests (crates/blaze-engine/tests/repro.rs): a_crate_rebuilds_after_its_daemon_restarts (deterministic, ~2 min), an_edited_crate_rebuilds_on_one_daemon. Quick check without the test binary: tools/v2/repro/repro.py check (see /tmp/blaze-lanes/v2-repro.md). This also blocks every reduction: the reducer keeps one daemon warm across candidates, and each candidate is an edit.

history.note: already in the tree: blaze-query segment.rs copy() grows cap until len fits, put() asserts the bounds in release too; test segment.rs a_copy_bigger_than_the_lanes_next_segment_still_fits_in_it. Added: Segments::new asserts first > 0 so the grow loop is bounded.
